t: This is St Botolph's Aldgate, a Church of England parish church just outside the line of the City's former eastern walls, so it counts as part of the East End. It served the ancient parish that included Portsoken Ward. George Dance the Elder, the City of London's surveyor, designed it. Many notable people are buried here. They include William Symington, builder of the first practical steamboat, and Thomas Bray, who helped establish the Church of England in Maryland. Two men from Henry VIII's reign, Lord Darcy and Sir Nicholas Carew, were both executed and are buried here. So is Sir John Cass, a merchant and MP who was a key figure in the Royal African Company, which was involved in the Atlantic slave trade.
